title: Life Support (ECLSS)
body: NASA's ECLSS recycles air and water so crews can live far from Earth without endless resupply. Every liter counts.

title: Mars Radiation
body: Curiosity's RAD instrument measured radiation on the way to Mars and on the surface — shielding is a real design choice.

title: Solar Flares (DONKI)
body: NASA's DONKI database tracks real solar flares and space weather. Flight teams use this kind of data when deciding if crews need extra shielding.

title: Dust vs Solar Power
body: Mars dust storms can dim sunlight for weeks. Solar-powered missions must plan for cloudy sols — just like your outpost.

title: Lunar Dust
body: Moon dust is sharp and clingy. It can cover solar panels and spacesuits. Artemis planners treat dust as a real engineering problem.

title: Power Off Earth
body: Many surface missions use solar arrays. Clear skies mean more watts for life support, science, and charging batteries for the night.

title: Growing Food in Space
body: NASA and partners study plant growth in space so crews might grow food farther from Earth. On Earth, the same ideas help remote communities.

title: Why Habitats Matter
body: A habitat is more than a room — it protects crew, stores supplies, and anchors life-support hardware.

title: Regolith Shielding
body: Covering habitats with local soil (regolith) is a studied way to add radiation protection without shipping heavy walls from Earth.

title: Recycling Water
body: On the ISS, water recyclers reclaim moisture from air and other sources so every drop matters.

title: Communication Delay
body: Radio to the Moon is about a second. To Mars it can be around 4 to 24 minutes one way. Crews must decide before Earth finishes talking.

title: Real Dose Rates (RadLab)
body: RadLab shares real radiation dose measurements from instruments in space. Your SHIELD meter is a kid-friendly stand-in for that kind of risk.

title: Space Biology (OSDR)
body: NASA's Open Science Data Repository holds research on how spaceflight affects living things — bones, sleep, plants, and more.

title: Real Mars Sites
body: Mars Trek lets you explore real elevation and imagery from NASA Mars missions — the same kind of place names used in your mission briefs.

title: Engineering Trade-offs
body: Every kilogram sent off Earth costs time and fuel. More greenhouse mass may mean less mass for shielding — choices matter.

title: Storing Energy
body: Batteries store daytime solar energy so systems keep running through the night — on the Moon or on Mars.

title: Junior Mission Control
body: Real missions balance life support, power, food, radiation, and delayed communications every day. You just practiced being a junior mission controller.
